title: PowerToys bug report, as per software prompt

judgment.rationale: The report contains a concrete FileNotFoundException for Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent 3.1.16.0 during PowerToys Run telemetry cleanup, but its version fields conflict (0.101.2362 versus attached 0.100.2.0). This supports a packaging/dependency investigation with a targeted fresh report.
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm the installed build and package contents, then fix or validate deployment of the TraceEvent dependency used by ETWTrace.

evidence.fact: The exception names Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent 3.1.16.0 and occurs in ETWTrace.Stop/Dispose during PowerLauncher shutdown.
The source ETWTrace class directly constructs and disposes TraceEventSession from Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent.
The issue body reports WinGet installation but contradictory product versions, so the failing package cannot yet be identified with confidence.

fix_assessment.rationale: The missing assembly is concrete, but the contradictory version metadata prevents choosing between stale installation, packaging omission, or upgrade residue.

proposed_fixes.title: Repair TraceEvent deployment and cleanup diagnostics
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The deployed PowerLauncher binary references Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent 3.1.16.0, but the assembly is absent or not loadable in the reported installation.
plan: Reproduce with the exact stable WinGet package and compare package contents to the ETWTrace assembly reference.
Fix the packaging/build dependency closure or, if packaging is correct, make cleanup report the dependency failure without masking the original application lifecycle.
Add an upgrade-path check for stale or incomplete dependency layouts.
verification: A clean install and upgrade install both load ETWTrace and shut down without the FileNotFoundException.
The published package contains the expected dependency next to the consuming binaries.
PowerToys Run startup and shutdown remain functional when telemetry recording is disabled.

confidence.rationale: The exception and consuming source are clear, but package/version ambiguity lowers confidence in the exact remediation.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run showed an error notification after an update because the TraceEvent assembly was unavailable while ETWTrace cleanup ran.
known_information: The issue reports WinGet installation and Windows build 26200.
The body says 0.101.2362.0 while the diagnostic text says 0.100.2.0.
The referenced assembly is a direct dependency of the repository ETWTrace implementation.
inferences: A package or upgrade-layout problem is more likely than a PowerToys Run query failure.
The exception may be surfaced during shutdown/cleanup rather than the original startup fault.
issue_context.analysis: Reconcile the actual installed version and inspect whether the published package contains the exact TraceEvent assembly expected by the deployed PowerToys binaries.

information_gaps.information: The exact installed PowerToys version and whether Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent.dll exists beside the failing binaries.
information_gaps.why_needed: The conflicting versions make it unsafe to attribute the failure to the current package or to an older upgrade residue.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce on the current stable WinGet package, record the About version, and run /bugreport immediately after the notification.

actions.label: Request targeted evidence
actions.note: Resolve the contradictory version/package evidence before changing dependency or cleanup behavior.

comment.body: The exception is specific: ETWTrace cleanup cannot load Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent 3.1.16.0. However, the issue body says 0.101.2362.0 while the attached diagnostic text says 0.100.2.0, so we cannot tell whether this is a current-package omission or stale files from an upgrade. Please confirm the version shown in PowerToys About, reproduce on the current WinGet package if possible, and run /bugreport immediately after the error. Do not upload private installation directories; the version and fresh report are sufficient.

actions.label: Approve focused fix design
actions.note: The proposed design is specific enough for fork-side implementation after maintainer approval.

design.scope: Validate and correct TraceEvent dependency packaging for the deployed PowerLauncher/ManagedTelemetry binaries, with cleanup behavior kept safe if the dependency is unavailable.
files: installer packaging project containing ManagedTelemetry dependencies
acceptance_criteria: The current WinGet package contains the exact TraceEvent assembly required by the deployed binaries.
Upgrade from the preceding stable version does not leave a missing dependency.
Telemetry cleanup does not surface an unhandled notification when telemetry recording is disabled or unavailable.
